title: Cough and cold
summary: Most colds pass in a week or two. Here is when a cough needs a call.
body: This guide is general information from a fictional practice, not medical advice. For your own symptoms, call the office.
home_signs: Rest and fluids|Honey in warm tea for adults and children over 1|A humidifier at night|Saline spray for stuffy noses
call_signs: Cough lasting more than 10 days|Fever that returns after a day or two of improvement|Symptoms that improve and then get worse
sameday_signs: Fever above 102°F for three days|Wheezing or a cough that keeps you awake for several nights|Ear pain or sinus pain with fever
now_signs: Trouble breathing at rest|Lips or face turning blue|Confusion or being very hard to wake

title: Sore throat
summary: Many sore throats are viral. A quick test tells us which ones are not.
body: A rapid strep test takes about ten minutes at the office. The nurse will ask about fever and swollen glands when you call.
home_signs: Warm fluids and lozenges for adults|Rest your voice
call_signs: Sore throat lasting more than 3 days|Known contact with strep
sameday_signs: Fever with swollen glands and no cough|Trouble swallowing liquids
now_signs: Drooling or unable to swallow|Trouble breathing or a muffled voice with stiff neck

title: Sprains and strains
summary: Ankle, wrist and back strains: rest, support and when to be seen.
body: Most sprains improve in one to two weeks. Our sports and work injury clinic runs Thursday mornings.
home_signs: Rest, ice and light compression|Raise the limb|Gentle movement as pain allows
call_signs: Pain not improving after a week|Swelling that keeps growing
sameday_signs: You cannot put weight on the limb|Numbness or a joint that gives way
now_signs: A bone visible through the skin|A limb that looks bent or is cold and pale

title: Rashes
summary: New rashes: what to note before you call, and which ones need a same-day look.
body: Take a clear photo in daylight before the call. The nurse may ask you to upload it to the patient area.
home_signs: Skip new soaps and lotions|Cool compresses for itch
call_signs: A rash lasting more than a week|A rash that keeps returning
sameday_signs: A rash with fever|A rash that spreads quickly
now_signs: A rash with swelling of the face or lips|Trouble breathing after a new medicine or food

title: High blood pressure follow-up
summary: Home readings, medicines and how often we check.
body: Bring your home log or the cuff itself; we check it against ours once a year.
home_signs: Take readings at the same time each day|Sit quietly for five minutes first|Write down each number
call_signs: Readings above your target for a week|Dizziness with a new medicine
sameday_signs: A reading above 180/120 with a headache and no other symptoms: call right away
now_signs: Chest pain|Sudden weakness on one side or trouble speaking

title: Diabetes checkup
summary: Checks we do each quarter and what to bring.
body: The A1C is a blood test that shows your average sugar over three months. We do it during the follow-up or at the lab draw.
home_signs: Keep your usual routine|Bring your meter or app readings
call_signs: Readings often above or below your range|Sores on the feet that do not heal
sameday_signs: Very high readings with thirst and tiredness|Vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
now_signs: Confusion or a very low reading that does not come up after treating it

title: Child with a fever
summary: Fevers in children: what to note, what to do and when to call us.
body: Call the same morning for any fever in a baby under 3 months.
home_signs: Fluids and rest|Light clothing|A fever alone does not need treatment if the child is comfortable
call_signs: Fever for more than 2 days|Ear pulling or a new rash
sameday_signs: Fever with a stiff neck or very sleepy child|Fewer wet diapers than usual
now_signs: Baby under 3 months with any fever|Trouble breathing or a seizure

title: Back pain
summary: Most back pain eases with gentle movement. Warning signs that need a visit.
body: Staying active helps more than bed rest. Our physical-therapy referral list is at the front desk.
home_signs: Gentle walking|Heat or ice, whichever feels better|Change positions often
call_signs: Pain lasting over 4 weeks|Pain that wakes you at night
sameday_signs: Pain after a fall|Pain with numbness down the leg
now_signs: Loss of bladder or bowel control|Weakness in both legs

title: Trouble sleeping
summary: Sleep habits, when to book a visit and when to call for help.
body: Sleep problems are common and often treatable. A provider will ask about stress, caffeine and medicines.
home_signs: Regular wake time|Dim screens an hour before bed|Skip caffeine after noon
call_signs: Poor sleep for more than 3 weeks|Loud snoring with daytime sleepiness
sameday_signs: Poor sleep with low mood|Panic attacks
now_signs: Thoughts of harming yourself: call or text 988 or go to the nearest emergency room

title: Low mood and stress
summary: When feeling low or stressed lasts, a visit can help.
body: Any provider can start the conversation. We use short questionnaires and can refer for counseling.
home_signs: Move your body daily|Talk to someone you trust|Keep a regular schedule
call_signs: Low mood most days for two weeks|Loss of interest in usual things
sameday_signs: Hard to work or care for family|Using alcohol or other substances to cope
now_signs: Thoughts of harming yourself: call or text 988 or go to the nearest emergency room
